lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: credit reports and scores

objective: Learners quantify the cost of an invented credit-standing difference over one year and over a full loan term.
scenario: Fionnuala is an invented eighth grader studying a pretend lending table. On a $15,000.00 invented auto loan, one borrower is offered 5.5% and another 12.9% for the simulated year, based only on recorded repayment history.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute one simulated year of interest at Fionnuala's lower invented rate of 5.5%.

prompts.text: How much interest does the 5.5% rate cost in a year?

tasks.directions: Compute the same year at 12.9%, then find the annual cost of the higher rate for Fionnuala.

prompts.text: How much interest does the 12.9% rate cost in a year?
What is the annual cost of the higher rate?

tasks.directions: Extend both of Fionnuala's rates across a five-year term on a simple-interest basis.

prompts.text: What does five years at 12.9% cost in interest?
How much more is that than five years at 5.5%?

tasks.directions: The two borrowers received identical vehicles.

prompts.text: Using Fionnuala's figures, explain what a repayment record is being used to predict and name two actions that would improve a borrower's standing.

remediation: If a learner compares percentages without computing, convert both of Fionnuala's rates to dollar figures on the same principal before comparing.
extension: Ask the learner what the higher-rate borrower would need to put down to pay the same total interest over five years.
